verdict: Avoid new unsecured exposure in Delhi professional services; lend only to cash-generative, retainer-backed firms with tight monthly monitoring.
title: Delhi Professional Services: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business actually is
Professional services here means people selling time and advice — IT/BPO delivery, staffing, consulting, accounting, design. Cash comes from contracts and retainers, not inventory; the balance sheet is receivables plus payroll. **The whole credit is a bet on collections and client concentration, not on assets.** Peer staffing shows the model's cash engine: 116 new contracts and highest-ever quarterly cash collection of ~₹4.3k Cr [4]. So when a proposal lands, check DSO and top-client share first; if one client is over a third of billings, ask for the contract term and renewal date.

## Where value and cash sit
Margin is set by billing rate minus salary, and pricing power is thin where work is commoditised. Firstsource grew revenue 22.2% YoY but EPS fell to ₹1.74 from ₹2.33 and margin to 4.9% from 7.6% on higher expenses [5][6]. **Growth without margin is the trap in this sector.** Working capital is the swing factor — ICRA notes longer cycles raise funding needs and shorter cycles improve liquidity [9]. So take receivables ageing every month; if DSO stretches beyond the contract's credit terms, ask which client and why.

## What has changed now
Delhi's local demand is running behind India: GST +2.7% Apr-to-date vs +6.1% national, and electricity demand +6.5% vs +9.5% [D]. **That is a local stress signal, and it is why the data call is AVOID (score 30) [D].** Nationally, bank credit is +20.0% YoY against activity of +6.1% [D] — money is chasing borrowers faster than business is growing. Separately, compulsory work-from-home in Delhi from Nov 5 to Nov 20 due to pollution [1] will thin office-based billing and shift costs to connectivity and home set-ups; ask how November utilisation is tracking.

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
Pursue staffing and BPO firms with multi-year contracts and demonstrated collections [4], and IT firms holding margins through AI spend [7]. Avoid pure body-shop consultants with single-client dependence and thin margins [5]. **Structure on receivables, not hope:** charge on collections, keep tenor inside contract life, and take monthly DSO, billing-vs-collection and top-five client concentration. Rating work flags partnership structures as vulnerable to partner withdrawals [10]; if the borrower is an LLP, ask for partner capital withdrawal history.

## Early-warning signs
- DSO rising two months running (monthly) -> ask for client-wise ageing and hold new limits.
- Billing minus collection gap widening (monthly) -> shift to collection-linked drawing power.
- Margin falling while revenue rises, as at Firstsource [5] (quarterly) -> reprice or reduce exposure.
- Client contract non-renewal or WFH-driven utilisation drop [1] (monthly) -> reassess limit.

Sources are thin on Delhi-specific professional-services data; the local read rests on the GST and power signals [D] plus peers. Rating methodology notes are undated and should be read as background, not current.

Revenue up but margin down (as peer [5]) -> reprice or trim exposure

Utilisation drop -> reassess limit and ask for cost pass-through
